skills.trigger: When evaluating a chest X-ray for signs of chronic pulmonary embolism or pulmonary hypertension and needing to distinguish vascular enlargement from other pathologies.
steps: Assess the caliber of the central pulmonary arteries, specifically looking for prominence or enlargement of the right descending pulmonary artery.

Systematically exclude alternative diagnoses by confirming the absence of pleural effusion (blunted costophrenic angles), wedge-shaped opacities (Hampton's hump), hilar lymphadenopathy, reticular interstitial patterns, and significant cardiomegaly.
Conclude that isolated central pulmonary artery prominence in the absence of these other findings supports a diagnosis of pulmonary hypertension secondary to chronic thromboembolic disease.
